sites.name: Arrastra Gulch Mining Corridor
overview: Historic mining corridor with early placer, mine, mill and tramway context; individual workings remain distinct.

sites.name: Big Giant Mine, Mill & Contention Tramway Complex
overview: Linked mine, mill and tramway complex retained as one parent identification record.

sites.name: Buffalo Boy–Vertex Mine, Mill & Aerial Tramway Complex
overview: Buffalo Boy/Vertex mine, mill and tramway landscape.

sites.name: Durango–Silverton Mining Railroad Corridor
overview: Historic narrow-gauge mining railroad corridor between Durango and Silverton.

sites.name: Eureka Mining Town
overview: Historic Eureka mining settlement; Sunnyside mine and mill components remain distinct.

sites.name: Frisco-Bagley Mill & Tunnel
overview: Historic Frisco-Bagley reduction mill and tunnel complex.

sites.name: Gladstone / Gold King Mining Camp
overview: Historic Gladstone mining camp linked to Gold King and American Tunnel but kept as a distinct town/camp identity.

sites.name: Maggie Gulch / Middleton–Hamlet–Intersection Mining Landscape
overview: Gulch-scale parent for the linked Middleton, Hamlet and Intersection mining landscape.

sites.name: Martin Mining Complex
overview: Historic Martin mining complex with preserved boardinghouse and transportation/mining context.

sites.name: Mayflower / Shenandoah-Dives Mill
overview: Historic selective-flotation mill; keep mine workings, tram and later operating phases as linked distinct components.

sites.name: Mogul–Grand Mogul Mine Complex
overview: Related Mogul and Grand Mogul mine sites retained as linked but distinct components.

sites.name: Pride of the West & Green Mountain Mines Complex
overview: Linked Pride of the West and Green Mountain mine complex.

sites.name: Silver Lake Mine & Mill
overview: Basin-level parent identification for the Silver Lake mine-and-mill landscape.

sites.name: Sound Democrat Mill & Mine
overview: Historic Sound Democrat mill-and-mine complex; Silver Queen remains a linked distinct component.

sites.name: Tobasco Mine & Mill
overview: Historic Tobasco mine-and-mill complex with identifiable processing ruins.

sites.name: Howardsville Mining Camp / Townsite
overview: Howardsville is an 1874 mining camp in the upper Animas district that served Cunningham Gulch mines and briefly functioned as the first San Juan County seat.

sites.location: Silverton–Animas Forks corridor, San Juan County, Colorado
sites.name: Silverton Northern Railroad / Animas Forks Line
overview: The Silverton Northern linked Silverton with Howardsville, Eureka, and Animas Forks; surviving engine-house and grade remnants identify this mining-transportation corridor.

sites.location: Animas Forks, San Juan County, Colorado
sites.name: Animas Forks Ghost Town
overview: Animas Forks is a documented high-elevation mining townsite with surviving buildings and a well-established nineteenth-century mining history.

sites.name: Silverton Historic Mining District
overview: Silverton is the historic center of the San Juan mining district and preserves a nationally significant mining-town landscape.

sites.name: Brooklyn Mine Complex
overview: The Brooklyn Mine is a documented historic mine in San Juan County's Silverton-area hard-rock mining landscape and retains recognizable mine buildings, waste rock, and associated industrial features.
The site is now also part of the broader Bonita Peak environmental-remediation landscape, which has altered portions of the historic mine setting.

timeline.text: The Bonita Peak Mining District, including the Brooklyn Mine site, was added to the federal National Priorities List for mine-related contamination.

sites.name: Highland Mary Mining Camp & Mine/Mill Complex
overview: Highland Mary was a substantial mining camp and mine-and-mill complex in Cunningham Gulch, with worker housing and processing facilities tied to a major silver-producing property.
The surviving landscape represents the linked camp, mine, mill, boarding-house, and transportation system rather than a single isolated opening.

timeline.text: The Highland Mary claim was staked.
A post office operated at Highland Mary, confirming the development of a distinct mining settlement.
New owners acquired the mine and renewed development.
The Highland Mary remained an important producer in the Silverton area.

sites.name: Lackawanna Mine & Mill Complex
overview: The Lackawanna complex linked a large flotation mill on the Animas River with mine workings in Swansea Gulch by aerial tram.
The surviving multi-story mill and associated industrial landscape preserve one of the clearest examples of twentieth-century ore processing around Silverton.

timeline.text: The surviving Lackawanna mill was constructed and began operating.
The mill operated for several decades, treating polymetallic ores.
Major tailings-removal work changed parts of the industrial landscape.

sites.name: North Star Mine & Mill / Sultan Mountain Complex
overview: The North Star Mine on Sultan Mountain was an important Silverton-area underground mine with a documented mill site and multiple portal levels.
The site preserves a combination of historic mine workings, mill remains, waste-rock landscape, and modern drainage or remediation infrastructure.

timeline.text: The North Star was among the important mines active during Silverton's early boom.
A substantial water-powered mill was developed for the property.
The Level 7 portal was closed or backfilled while mine drainage was maintained.
Modern stabilization and remediation work altered portions of the waste-rock and drainage landscape.

sites.name: Sunnyside Mine & American Tunnel Complex
overview: The Sunnyside Mine and American Tunnel form a linked but physically distinct mining and haulage system in the Silverton-area district.
The American Tunnel began as a Gold King Mine project and was later extended beneath Bonita Peak to provide low-level haulage and drainage access for the revived Sunnyside operation.

timeline.text: Development of the Sunnyside Mine began.
Work began on the American Tunnel beneath the Gold King Mine.
Standard Metals extended the American Tunnel to connect with the Sunnyside system.
The Lake Emma water inflow temporarily shut the Sunnyside operation.
